πᾶς.g: all, the whole, every kind of
πᾶς.long: all, the whole, every kind of.
πᾶς.kj: all (manner of, means), alway(-s), any (one), X daily, + ever, every (one, way), as many as, + no(-thing), X thoroughly, whatsoever, whole, whosoever
πᾶς.der: including all the forms of declension; apparently a primary word;
πᾶς.as:
πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν, gen., παντός, πάσης, παντός,
[in LXX chiefly for כֹּל;]
all, every.
I. As adj.,
1. c. subst. anarth., all, every, of every kind: Mt 3:104:23, Mk 9:49, Lk 4:37, Jo 2:10, Ac 27:20, Ro 7:8, Re 18:17, al. mult.; pl., all, Ac 22:15, Ro 5:12, He 1:6, al.; of the highest degree, π. ἐξουσία (προθυμία, χαρά), Mt 28:18, Ac 17:11, Phl 2:29, al.; also the whole (though in this sense more freq. c. art.), Mt 2:3, Ac 2:36, Ro 11:26.
2. C. art. (before the art., after the noun, or, denoting totality, between the art. and noun), all, whole: Mt 8:3213:2, Mk 5:33, Lk 1:10, Ac 7:14, Ro 3:19, Ga 5:14, Eph 4:16, al.; pl., Mt 2:4, Mk 4:13, Ro 1:5, al.
II. As pron.,
1. masc. and fem., every one: Mk 9:49, Lk 16:16, He 2:9; seq. rel. pron., Mt 7:24, Ac 2:21, Ga 3:10, al.; c. ptcp. (anarth.), Mt 13:19, Lk 11:4; c. ptcp. (c. art.), Mt 5:22, Mk 7:8, Lk 6:47, Jo 3:8, Ro 1:16, al.; pl., πάντες, absol., all, all men, Mt 10:22, Mk 13:13, Lk 20:38, Jo 1:73:26, I Co 8:1, al.; οἱ π. (collectively, as a definite whole), Ro 11:32, I Co 1:17, Eph 4:13, al.; π. οἱ (ὅσοι), Mt 4:24, Mk 1:32, Lk 4:40, al.
2. Neut.,
(a) sing., πᾶν, everything, all: πᾶν τό, c. ptcp., I Co 10:25, 27, Eph 5:13, I Jo 2:165:4 (sc. ὄν); πᾶν ὅ, Jo 17:2, Ro 14:23; collectively, of persons (Westc., in l.), Jo 6:37, 39; c. prep., in adverbial phrases, διὰ παντός, always, Mt 18:10, al.; ἐν παντί, in everything, in every way, II Co 4:8, Phl 4:6, al.;
(b) pl., πάτνα, all things: absol., Jo 1:3, I Co 2:10, He 2:8, al.; of certain specified things, Mk 4:34, Lk 1:3, Ro 8:28, I Th 5:21, al.; acc., πάντα, adverbially, wholly, in all things, in all respects, Ac 20:35, I Co 9:25, al.; c. art., τὰ π., all things (a totality, as distinct from anarth. πάντα, all things severally; cf. Westc., Eph., 186 f.), absol.: Ro 11:36, I Co 8:6, Eph 3:9, He 1:3, al.; relatively, Mk 4:11, Ac 17:25, Ro 8:32, al.; πάντα τά, c. ptcp., Mt 18:31, al.; πάντα ταῦτα (ταῦτα π.), Mt 6:32, 33, al.; πάντα, c. prep, in adverbial phrases, πρὸ πάντων, above all things, Ja 5:12, I Pe 4:8; ἐν π., in all things, in all ways, I Ti 3:11, I Pe 4:11, al.; κατὰ πάντα, in all respects, Ac 17:22, al.
3. C. neg., πᾶς οὐ (μή) = οὐδείς, v.s. οὐ and μή, and cf. M, Pr., 245 f.

παραλαμβάνω.long: I take from, receive from, or: I take to, receive (apparently not used of money), admit, acknowledge; I take with me.
παραλαμβάνω.sd: to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation); by analogy, to assume an office; figuratively, to learn
παραλαμβάνω.as:
παρα-λαμβάνω,
[in LXX chiefly for לקח, also for ירשׁ, etc.;]
1. c. acc. rei, like παραδέχομαι, correl. to παραδίδωμι, to receive from another: Col 4:17, He 12:28; of the mind, I Co 11:2315:1, 3, Ga 1:9, Phl 4:9; c. inf., Mk 7:4; seq. παρά, c. gen., Ga 1:12, I Th 2:134:1, II Th 3:6; τ. Χριστόν (Lft., in l.), Col 2:6.
2. C. acc. pers., to take to or with oneself: Mt 2:13, 14, 20, 2117:126:37, Mk 4:365:409:210:32, Lk 9:10, 2811:2618:31Jo 19:16, Ac 15:3923:18; γυναῖκα, Mt 1:20, 24; μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ, Mt 12:4518:16, Mk 14:33; seq. εἰς, Mt 4:5, 827:27; κατ’ ἰδίαν, Mt 20:17; mid., seq. πρὸς ἐμαυτόν, Jo 14:3; pass., Mt 24:40, 41, Lk 17:34-36; ptcp., prefixed to other verbs (Bl, § 74, 2), Ac 16:3321:24, 26, 32; metaph., Jo 1:11.†

παρθένος.long: a maiden, virgin; extended to men who have not known women.
παρθένος.sd: a maiden; by implication, an unmarried daughter
παρθένος.as:
παρθένος, -ου, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for בְּתוּלָה, Ex 22:16 (15), Jb 31:1, Is 23:4, al.; also for נַעַר, נַעֲרָה, Ge 24:14, 16, 5534:3, and for עַלְמָה, Ge 24:43, Is 7:14;]
a maiden, virgin: Mt 1:23(LXX)25:1, 7, 11, Lk 1:27, Ac 21:9, I Co 7:25 ff., II Co 11:2; masc., of chaste persons (CIG, 8784 b): Re 14:4.†

παραγίνομαι.long: (a) I come on the scene, appear, come, (b) with words expressing destination: I present myself at, arrive at, reach.
παραγίνομαι.sd: to become near, i.e. approach (have arrived); by implication, to appear publicly
παραγίνομαι.as:
παρα-γίνομαι
(Ion. and late for -γίγν-), [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא;]
1.to be beside or at hand (Hom., Hdt., al.), hence, to stand by, support (Æsch., Thuc., al.): c. dat. pers., II Ti 4:16.
2.to come, come up, arrive (Hdt., Xen., al., and freq. in later writers; v. MM, xviii; Thackeray, Gr., 2672): absol., Lk 14:2119:16, Jo 3:23, Ac 5:21, 22, 259:3910:32, 3311:2314:2717:1018:2721:1823:16, 3524:17, 2425:728:21, I Co 16:3; seq. εἰς, Jo 8:2, Ac 9:2615:4; ἐπί, c. acc., Lk 22:52; πρός, c. acc., Lk 7:4, 208:19, Ac 20:18; id. seq. ἐκ, Lk 11:6; παρά, c. gen., Mk 14:43; ἀπὸ . . . εἰς, Mt 2:1, Ac 13:14; ἀπὸ . . . ἐπὶ . . . πρός, Mt 3:13; of a teacher coming forward in public: Mt 3:1, Lk 12:51, He 9:11.†

παρά.long: gen: from; dat: beside, in the presence of; acc: alongside of.
παρά.sd: properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of)
παρά.kj: above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side…by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with
παρά.as:
παρά, prep. c. gen., dat., acc.,
with radical sense, beside.
I. C. gen. pers., from the side of, from beside, from, indicating source or origin, [in LXX for מֵאֵצֶל, מִיַד, מִלִּפְנֵי;] after verbs of motion, Mk 14:43, Lk 8:49, Jo 15:26, al.; after verbs of seeking, receiving, hearing, etc., Mk 8:1112:2, Jo 4:9, 5210:18, Phl 4:18, II Ti 1:18, Ja 1:7, al.; after passive verbs, of the agent (like ὑπό), Mt 21:42, Mk 12:11, Lk 1:37; absol., οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ, his family, his kinsfolk, Mk 3:21 (cf. M, Pr., 106 f.; Field, Notes, 25 f.; Swete, in l.); τὰ παρ’ αὐτῆς (αὐτῶν, ὑμῶν), one's means, wealth, Mk 5:26, Lk 10:7, Phl 4:18.
II. C. dat. pers. (exc. Jo 19:25, π. τ. σταυρῷ), by the side of, beside, by, with, [in LXX for בְּעֵינֵי, בְּיַד, אֵצֶל;] Lk 11:3719:7, Jo 1:404:40, Ac 28:14, al.; παρ’ ἑαυτῷ, at home, I Co 16:2; c. dat. pl., among, Mt 22:25, Col 4:16, al.; metaph., Mt 19:26, Mk 10:27, Lk 1:30, Ro 2:13, Ja 1:27, al.
III. C. acc., of motion by or towards, [in LXX for בְּעֵבֶר ,עַל יַד ,אֵצֶל;]
1. of place, by the side of, beside, by, along: Ac 10:32, He 11:12; after verbs of motion, Mt 4:18, Mk 4:4, Lk 8:5, Ac 4:35, al.; after verbs of rest, Mt 13:1, Mk 5:21, Lk 8:35, al.
2.beside, beyond, metaph.;
(a)beyond, against, contrary to: Ac 18:13, Ro 1:264:1811:24, al.; except, II Co 11:24;
(b)beyond, above, in comparison with: Lk 3:13, Ro 12:314:5, He 1:4, 93:3, al.;
(c)on account of: I Co 12:15, 16.
IV. In composition: beside, to (παραλαμβάνω, παράγω), at hand (πάρειμι), from (παραρρέω), amiss (παρακούω), past (παρέρχομαι), compared with (παρομοιάζω), above measure (παροργίζω).

παιδίον.long: a little child, an infant, little one.
παιδίον.sd: a childling (of either sex), i.e. (properly), an infant, or (by extension) a half-grown boy or girl; figuratively, an immature Christian
παιδίον.as:
παιδίον, -ου, τό,
dimin, of παῖς, [in LXX chiefly for יֶלֶד, also for נַעַר, בֵּן, etc., freq. in To in ref. to full-grown youth;]
a young child, a little one: Mt 2:8, 9, 11, ff., Lk 1:59, 66, 76, 802:17, 27, 40, Jo 16:21, He 11:23; of older children, Mt 18:2, 4, 5, Mk 5:39-417:309:24, 36, Lk 9:47, 4818:17, Jo 4:49; in pl., Mt 11:1614:2115:3818:319:13, 14, Mk 7:2810:13 ff., Lk 7:3211:718:16, He 2:13, 14 Metaph., I Co 14:20. Colloq. in familiar address (as Eng. colloq., "lads"—v. M, Pr., 170n—and Irish use of "boys"): Jo 21:5, I Jo 2:13, 183:7.†
SYN.: v.s. παῖς.

παῖς.long: (a) a male child, boy, (b) a male slave, servant; thus: a servant of God, especially as a title of the Messiah, (c) a female child, girl.
παῖς.sd: a boy (as often beaten with impunity), or (by analogy), a girl, and (genitive case) a child; specially, a slave or servant (especially a minister to a king; and by eminence to God)
παῖς.kj: child, maid(-en), (man) servant, son, young man
παῖς.as:
παῖς, gen., παιδός, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for עֶבֶד, also for נַעַר, נַעֲרָה, etc.;]
1.a child, boy, youth, maiden: ὁ π., Mt 17:18, Lk 2:439:42, Ac 20:12; ἡ π.Lk 8:51, 54 (on the artic. nom, of address, v. M, Pr., 70 f., 235; Bl., § 33, 4); pl., Mt 2:1621:15; of parentage, c. gen., Jo 4:51.
2. Like Heb. עֶבֶד, Lat. puer, Fr. garçon, Eng. boy (Æsch., Aristoph., Xen., al.), servant, slave, attendant: Mt 8:6, 8, 13, Lk 7:712:4515:26; in late writers (Diod., LXX: Ge 41:37, al.), of a king's attendant or minister: Mt 14:2; so (= Heb. עֶבֶדיְהֹוָה) π. τ. θεοῦ (Ps 66 (69):18, Is 41:8, Wi 2:13, al.), of Israel, Lk 1:54; of David, Lk 1:69, Ac 4:25; of Jesus (but v. Dalman, Words, 277 f.), Mt 12:18(LXX), Ac 3:13, 264:27, 30.†
SYN.: 1. τέκνον, child, with emphasis on parentage and the consequent community of nature; υἱός, son, with emphasis on the privileged position of heirship; π. refers both to age and parentage, but with emphasis on the former. Cf. also παιδάριον, παιδίον, παιδίσκη, and v. Westc. on I Jo 3:1. 2. v.s. θεράπων, and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 7 f.

παρακαλέω.long: (a) I send for, summon, invite, (b) I beseech, entreat, beg, (c) I exhort, admonish, (d) I comfort, encourage, console.
παρακαλέω.sd: to call near, i.e. invite, invoke (by imploration, hortation or consolation)
παρακαλέω.kj: beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort(-ation), intreat, pray
παρακαλέω.as:
παρα-καλέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for נחם ni., pi.;]
1.to call to one, call for, summon: Ac 28:20 (R, mg.; R, txt., entreat); hence (of the gods: Dem., Xen., al.), to invoke, call on, beseech, entreat: τ. πατέρα μου, Mt 26:53; τ. κύριον, II Co 12:8; in late writers (Polyb., Diod., al.; rarely in LXX; in π., v. Deiss., LAE, 17614), also of men: absol., Phm 9; c. acc., Mt 8:5, Mk 1:40, Ac 16:9, al.; c. inf., Mk 5:17, Lk 8:41, Ac 8:31, al.; seq. ἵνα (v. M, Pr., 205, 208), Mt 14:36, Mk 5:18, Lk 8:31, al.
2.to admonish, exhort: absol., Lk 3:18, Ro 12:8, II Ti 4:2, al.; c. acc., Ac 15:32, I Th 2:11, He 3:13, al.; id. seq. inf., Ac 11:23, Ro 12:1, Phl 4:2, I Th 4:10, al.; seq. ἵνα (v. M, Pr., 205, 208), I Co 1:10, II Co 8:6, I Th 4:1, al.
3.to cheer, encourage, comfort (Plut., LXX: Jb 4:3, Is 35:3, Si 43:24, al.): c. acc., II Co 1:6, Eph 6:22, Col 2:2, al.; id. seq. ἐν, I Th 4:18; διά, II Co 1:4; pass., Mt 5:4, Lk 16:25, Ac 20:12.
SYN.: παραμυθέω (cf. M, Th., 25).

πατήρ.sd: a "father" (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)
πατήρ.as:
πατήρ, πατρός, -τρί, τέρα,
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for אָב;]
a father;
1. prop.,
(a) of the male parent: Mt 2:22, Lk 1:17, Jo 4:53; anarth., He 12:7 (M, Pr., 82 f.); pl., of both parents (cl.), He 11:23; οἱ π. τ. σαρκός, He 12:9;
(b) of a forefather or ancestor (in cl. usually in pl.; Hom., al.): Mt 3:9, Lk 1:73, Jo 8:39, al.; pl., Mt 23:30, 32, Lk 6:23, 26, Jo 4:20, I Co 10:1, al.
2. Metaph.,
(a) of an author, originator, or archetype (= αἴτιος, ἀρχηγός, etc.; Pind., Plat., al.): Jo 8:41-44, Ro 4:11, 12, 16.
(b) as a title of respect or honour, used of seniors, teachers and others in a position of responsible authority (Jg 17:10, II Ki 2:12, Pr 1:8, al.): Mt 23:9, Ac 7:222:1, I Jo 2:13.
3. Of God (as in cl. of Zeus) as Father;
(a) of created things: τ. φώτων, Ja 1:17;
(b) of all sentient beings: Eph 3:14, 15, He 12:9;
(c) of men, esp. those in covenant relation with Him (freq in OT and later Jewish lit.; v. Dalman, Words, 184 ff.): Mt 6:4, Lk 6:36, Jo 4:21, Ja 3:9, al.; ὁ π. ὁ ἐν (τ.) οὐρανοῖς, Mt 5:16, Mk 11:25; ὁ π. ὁ οὐράνιος, Mt 6:1415:13; esp. in the Epp., of Christians: Ro 8:15, II Co 6:18, Ga 4:6, Eph 2:184:6, I Jo 2:1; c. gen. qual., τ. οἰκτιρμῶν, II Co 1:3; τ. δοξῆς, Eph 1:17;
(d) of Christ (Dalman, Words, 190 ff.);
(α) by our Lord himself: ὁ π., Mt 11:25-27, Lk 10:21, 22, Jo 5:20-23, al.; ὁ π. μου, Mt 11:27, al.; ὁ ἐν τ. οὐρανοῖς, Mt 7:11, al.; ὁ οὐράνιος, Mt 15:13; vocat., Jo 11:4112:27, 2817:1, 5, 11, 20, 25 (cf. Abbott, JG., 96 f.);
(β) by Apostles: Jo 1:14 (anarth.; v. M, Pr., 82 f.), Ro 15:6, II Co 1:311:31, Eph 1:3, Col 1:3, He 1:5, I Pe 1:3, Re 1:6 (cf. Westc., Epp. Jo., 27-34).

πάλιν.g: again, further, on the other hand
πάλιν.long: again, back, once more, further, on the other hand.
πάλιν.sd: (adverbially) anew, i.e. (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjunctionally) furthermore or on the other hand
πάλιν.der: probably from the same as G3823 (πάλη) (through the idea of oscillatory repetition);
πάλιν.as:
πάλιν, adv.,
[in LXX for שׁוּב, etc.;]
1. of place, back, backwards (LS, s.v.).
2. Of time, again, once more: Mt 4:8, Mk 2:13, Lk 23:20, Jo 1:35 (and freq.), Ac 17:32, Ro 11:23, Ga 1:9, He 1:6, al; pleonastically, π. ἀνακάμπτειν, Ac 18:21; ὑποστρέφειν, Ga 1:17; εἰς τὸ π., II Co 13:2; π. ἐκ τρίτου (Bl., § 81, 4), Mt 26:44; ἐκ δευτέρου, Mt 26:42, Ac 10:15; π. δεῦτερον, Jo 4:5421:16; π. ἄνωθεν ( Wi 19:6), Ga 4:9.
3. Rhetorically, again;
(a)further, moreover: Mt 5:33, Lk 13:20, Jo 12:39, al.;
(b)in turn, on the other hand (Soph.; LXX: Wi 13:816:23, al.): Lk 6:43, I Co 12:21, II Co 10:7, I Jo 2:8.

παραδίδωμι.long: I hand over, pledge, hand down, deliver, commit, commend, betray, abandon.
παραδίδωμι.sd: to surrender, i.e yield up, intrust, transmit
παραδίδωμι.kj: betray, bring forth, cast, commit, deliver (up), give (over, up), hazard, put in prison, recommend
παραδίδωμι.as:
παρα-δίδωμι,
[in LXX chiefly for נתן;] correl. to παρδέχομαι,
1.to give or hand over to another: c. acc. et dat., Mt 11:2725:14, Lk 4:6, al.; of being delivered up to a course of teaching, pass. seq. εἰς, Ro 6:17.
2.to commit, commend: Ac 14:2615:40, I Pe 2:23.
3.to give or deliver up to prison or judgment: c. acc. pers., Mt 4:12, Mk 1:14, Ro 4:25, II Pe 2:4; id. seq. ὑπέρ, Ro 8:32; c. dat., Mt 5:25, Mk 15:1, Lk 12:58, Jo 19:11, al.; id. seq. ἵνα, Jo 19:16; c. inf., Ac 12:4; seq. εἰς, Mt 10:1717:2224:9, Lk 21:12, Ac 8:3, II Co 4:11, al.; τ. Σατανᾷ, I Ti 1:20; id. seq. εἰς ὄλεθρον σαρκός, I Co 5:5; with the collat. idea of treachery (= προδίδωμι), c. acc. pers., Mt 26:16, Mk 14:11, Jo 6:64, al.; id. c. dat., Mt 26:15, al.; pres. ptcp., ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτόν, Mt 26:25, Mk 14:42, Jo 13:11.
4.to hand down, hand on or deliver verbally (traditions, commands, etc.): Mk 7:13, Lk 1:2, Ac 6:14, I Co 11:215:2; pass., II Pe 2:21, Ju 3.
5.to permit (for exx. in cl., v. LS, s.v.): Mk 4:29.

παραθαλάσσιος.as:
παρα-θαλάσσιος, -α, -ον
(< παρά, θάλασσα), [in LXX: Je 29 (47):7 (היָּםחוֹף), etc.;]
by the sea: Mt 4:13.†

παραλυτικός.as:
*† παρα-λυτικός, -ή, -όν
(< παραλύω),
paralytic: Mt 4:248:69:2, 6, Mk 2:3-5, 9, 10, Lk 5:24 (Rec., WH, mg.).†

παρέρχομαι.long: I pass by, pass away, pass out of sight; I am rendered void, become vain, neglect, disregard.
παρέρχομαι.sd: to come near or aside, i.e. to approach (arrive), go by (or away), (figuratively) perish or neglect, (causative) avert
παρέρχομαι.kj: come (forth), go, pass (away, by, over), past, transgress
παρέρχομαι.as:
παρ-έρχομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for עבר;]
1.to pass, pass by;
(a) of persons: absol., Lk 18:37; c. acc. pers., Mk 6:48; c. acc. lot., Ac 16:8; seq. διά, c. gen., Mt 8:28;
(b) of things: τ. ποτήριον, Mt 26:39 (ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ), Mt 26:42; of time, Mt 14:15, Mk 14:35, Ac 27:9, I Pe 4:3. Metaph.,
(a)to pass away, perish: Mt 5:1824:34, 35, Mk 13:30, 31, Lk 16:1721:32, 33, II Co 5:17, Ja 1:10, II Pe 3:10;
(b)to pass by, neglect, disregard: c. acc. rei, Lk 11:4215:29.
2.to come to, arrive: Lk 12:3717:7, Ac 24:7, R, mg. (cf. ἀντι-παρέρχομαι).†
SYN.: παραβαίνω.

παρεκτός.long: (a) adv. used as adj: besides, outside, without, left over, in addition, (b) prep: apart from, except.
παρεκτός.as:
**† παρ-εκτός, = cl. παρέκ, -έξ,
[in Aq.: De 1:36; Al., Le 23:38*;]
1. as adv., besides, in addition: τὰ π. (sc. γινόμενα), II Co 11:28.
2. As prep. c. gen., except: Mt 5:3219:9 (WH, mg., R, mg.), Ac 26:29.†

παράπτωμα.long: a falling away, lapse, slip, false step, trespass, sin.
παράπτωμα.sd: a side-slip (lapse or deviation), i.e. (unintentional) error or (wilful) transgression
παράπτωμα.as:
† παρά-πτωμα, -τος, τό
(< παραπίπτω), [in LXX for מַעַל, פֶּשַׁע, etc.;]
1.a false step, a blunder (Polyb.).
2. Ethically, a misdeed, trespass (LXX): Mt 6:14, 15, Mk 11:25, 26, Ro 4:255:15 ff. Ro 11:11, 12, II Co 5:19, Ga 6:1, Eph 1:72:1, 5, Col 2:13.†
SYN.: v.s. ἁμαρτία.

παράγω.g: I pass by, depart, pass away
παράγω.long: I pass by, depart, pass away.
παράγω.sd: to lead near, i.e. (reflexively or intransitively) to go along or away
παράγω.as:
παρ-άγω,
[in LXX chiefly for עבר;]
1. trans., to lead by, lead aside, lead into, lead forward, etc.
2. Intrans.,
(a)to pass by: Mt 9:9, 2720:30, Mk 2:1415:21, Jo 8:59 R, txt., 9:1; seq. παρό, c. acc., Mk 1:16;
(b)to go away, depart; metaph., to pass away: I Co 7:31; mid., I Jo 2:8, 17.†

παλαιός.long: old, ancient, not new or recent.
παλαιός.sd: antique, i.e. not recent, worn out
παλαιός.as:
παλαιός, -ά, -όν
(< πάλαι), [in LXX: Le 25:2226:10, Ca 7:13 (14) (ישׁן), Jos 9:4, 5, Je 45 (38):11 (בָּלֶה), etc.;]
old, ancient; opp. to νέος, καινός: οἶνος, Lk 5:39; διαθήκη, II Co 3:14; ἐντολή, I Jo 2:7; ζύμη, I Co 5:7, 8; ὁ π. ἄςθρωπος (for similar phrases, v. Westc., Eph., 68), Ro 6:6, Eph 4:22, Col 3:9; neut. pl., καινὰ καὶ π., Mt 13:52; of things not merely old, but worn by use (as Jos 9:4, 5, LXX), Mt 9:16, 17, Mk 2:21, 22, Lk 5:36, 37.†
SYN.: v.s. ἀρχαῖος.

παραγγέλλω.long: I notify, command, charge, entreat solemnly.
παραγγέλλω.sd: to transmit a message, i.e. (by implication) to enjoin
παραγγέλλω.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος);
παραγγέλλω.as:
παρ-αγγέλλω
(< παρά, ἀγγὲλλω), [in LXX for שׁמע pi., hi., etc.;]
1.to transmit a message (Æsch., Eur.).
2.to order, command (Hdt., Xen., al.): c. inf., Ac 15:5; c. acc. rei, I Co 11:17, II Th 3:4, I Ti 4:115:7; seq. ἵνα (M, Pr., 207; Bl., § 69, 4), Mk 6:8, II Th 3:12; c. dat. pers., Ac 17:30 R, txt., I Th 4:11; seq. λέγων, Mt 10:5; c. inf. aor., Mt 15:35, Mk 8:6, Lk 8:29, Ac 10:4216:18 (aoristic pres.; v. M, Pr., 119); id. c. neg., μή, Lk 5:148:56, Ac 23:22, I Co 7:10; c. inf. pres., Ac 16:23, II Th 3:6; id. c. neg., μή, Lk 9:21, Ac 1:44:185:28, 40, I Ti 1:36:17; c. acc., τοῦτο, seq. ὅτι (B1., § 70, 3), II Th 3:10; c. acc. et inf., Ac 23:30, II Th 3:6, I Ti 6:13 (Bl., § 72, 5).†
SYN.: v.s. ἐντέλλω.

πάλαι.long: of old, long ago, in times past, former.
πάλαι.sd: (adverbially) formerly, or (by relatively) sometime since; (elliptically as adjective) ancient
πάλαι.kj: any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past
πάλαι.der: probably another form for G3825 (πάλιν) (through the idea of retrocession);
πάλαι.as:
πάλαι,
adv. of time,
[in LXX: Is 48:5, 7 (מֵאָז), etc.;]
long ago, of old, in time past (denoting past time absolutely, as πρότερον relatively): Mt 11:21, Lk 10:13, He 1:1, Ju 4; as adj., c. art., II Pe 1:9; of time just past, Mk 6:47 (WH, mg.), 15:44 (WH, mg., R, txt.); c. durat. praes. (RV, all this time), II Co 12:19.†

παραβολή.long: (a) a comparison, (b) a parable, often of those uttered by our Lord, (c) a proverb, an adage.
παραβολή.sd: a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage
παραβολή.as:
παραβολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< παραβάλλω), [in LXX (cf. McNeile, Mt., 185): Nu 23:7, De 28:37, Ps 43 (44):14, Pr 1:6, Ez 12:22, al. (מָשָׁל), Si 47:17 (חִידָה), al. mutt. in Si, Wi 5:3;]
1.a placing beside, juxtaposition (Polyb., al.).
2.a comparing, comparison (Plat., Arist., al.).
3.a comparison, illustration, analogy, figure (Arist., al.): Mt 24:32, Mk 3:23, He 9:911:19; specif. of the pictures and narratives drawn from nature and human life which are characteristic of the synoptic teaching of our Lord, a parable: Mt 13:3, 10, Mk 4:2, 10, Lk 8:4, 9-11, al.; c. gen. ref., Mt 13:18, 36.
4 Like Heb. מָשָׁל (I Ki 10:12, Pr 1:6, Si 3:29, al.), = παροιμία, a proverb or gnomic saying: Lk 4:235:366:39.
SYN.: παροιμία (v. Abbott, Essays, 82 ff.).

παχύνομαι.long: I fatten, thicken; pass. fig: I become stupid, dull, unfeeling.
παχύνομαι.sd: to thicken, i.e. (by implication) to fatten (figuratively, stupefy or render callous)
παχύνομαι.der: from a derivative of G4078 (πήγνυμι) (meaning thick);
παχύνομαι.as:
παχύνω
(< παχύς, thick), [in LXX: De 32:15, Is 6:10 (שָׁמֵן), al.;]
to thicken, fatten; pass., to grow fat. Metaph., to make dull or stupid (τ. ψυχάς, Plut.); pass., to wax gross: ἡ καρδία, Mt 13:15, Ac 28:27 (LXX).†

παρατίθημι.g: I set before, serve, entrust to
παρατίθημι.long: (a) I set (especially a meal) before, serve, (b) act. and mid: I deposit with, entrust to, (c) I bring forward, quote as evidence.
παρατίθημι.sd: to place alongside, i.e. present (food, truth); by implication, to deposit (as a trust or for protection)
παρατίθημι.kj: allege, commend, commit (the keeping of), put forth, set before
παρατίθημι.as:
παρα-τίθημι,
[in LXX chiefly for שׂוּם;]
I. Act., to place beside, set before, c. acc. et dat.: of food, Mk 6:418:6, 7, Lk 9:1611:6; τράπεζαν, Ac 16:34; pass. ptcp., Lk 10:8, I Co 10:27; metaph., of teaching, παραβολήν, Mt 13:24, 31.
II. Mid.,
1.to have set before one (Hom., Thuc., Xen., al.).
2.to deposit with another, give in charge or commit to (Hdt., Xen., Polyb., al.) : c. acc. et dat., Lk 12:4823:46, Ac 14:2320:32, I Ti 1:18, II Ti 2:2, I Pe 4:19.
3.to bring forward, quote as evidence: seq. ὅτι, Ac 17:3 (v. Page, in l.).†

πατρίς.sd: a father-land, i.e. native town; (figuratively) heavenly home
πατρίς.as:
πατρίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(< πατήρ), [in LXX chiefly for מוֹלֶדֶת;] prop. poët. fern. of πάτριος,
of one's fathers; as subst., ἡ π. = πάτρα, fatherland, country, home, native place: Ac 18:27, WH, mg., He 11:14; of one's own town, Mt 13:54, 57, Mk 6:1, 4, Lk 4:23, 24, Jo 4:44.†

παραβαίνω.sd: to go contrary to, i.e. violate a command
παραβαίνω.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G939 (βάσις);
παραβαίνω.as:
παρα-βαίνω,
[in LXX for סוּר, עבר, פּרר hi., שׂטה, etc.;]
1. in Hom. (twice), to go by the side of, stand beside.
2. In Æsch., Herod., Thuc., al., to go past or pass over, chiefly metaph., to overstep, violate, transgress (Jos 7:11, Ez 16:59, Si 40:14, al.): τ. παράδοσιν, Mt 15:2; τ. ἐντολήν, Mt 15:3; seq. ἀπό (as סוּרמִן, De 17:20, al.), to turn aside, fall away (cf. π. τῆς ἀληθείας, Arist., Cael., i, 5, 2): Ac 1:25.†

παράδοσις.sd: transmission, i.e. (concretely) a precept; specially, the Jewish traditionary law
παράδοσις.as:
παρά-δοσις, -εως, ἡ
(< παραδίδωμι), [in LXX: Es 7:26 (אֱסוּר), Je 39 (32):4 (נתן ni.), Je 41 (34):2*;]
1.a handing down or over, transfer, transmission (Arist., Polyb., al., LXX).
2.tradition of doctrine (Plat., Epict., al.); by meton., of the doctrine itself : Mt 15:2, 3, 6, Mk 7:3 ff., I Co 11:2, Ga 1:14, Col 2:8, II Th 2:153:9.†

πάσχω.long: I am acted upon in a certain way, either good or bad; I experience ill treatment, suffer.
πάσχω.sd: to experience a sensation or impression (usually painful)
πάσχω.as:
πάσχω,
[in LXX: Am 6:6 (חלה ni.), Wi 12:27, Si 38:16, al.;]
to suffer, be acted on, as opp. to acting, often limited by a word expressive of good or evil;
(a) of misfortunes (most freq. without any limiting word): absol., Lk 22:1524:46, Ac 1:33:1817:3, I Co 12:26, He 2:189:2613:12, I Pe 2:19, 20, 233:174:15, 19; seq. ὑπό, c. gen., Mt 17:12; ὑπέρ, Ac 9:16, Phl 1:20, II Th 1:5, I Pe 2:21; c. dat. ref., I Pe 4:1; περί, c. gen. (seq. ὑπέρ), I Pe 3:18; διά, c. acc., I Pe 3:14; ὀλίγον (a little while), I Pe 5:10; c. acc., Mt 27:19, Mk 9:12, Lk 13:224:26, Ac 28:5, II Ti 1:12, He 5:8, Re 2:10; παθήματα, II Co 1:6; ταῦτα, Ga 3:4 (EV; cf. Lft., in l., but v. infr.); acc. seq. ἀπό, Mt 16:21, Lk 9:2217:25; ὑπό, Mk 5:26, I Th 2:14;
(b) of pleasant experiences (but always with qualifying word, εὖ or acc. rei) : Ga 3:4 (cf. Grimm-Thayer, s.v.; Interp. Com., in l., but v. supr.) (cf. προ-, συν-πάσχω).†

παρακούω.g: I refuse to hear, disobey, disregard
παρακούω.long: (a) I hear carelessly or incidentally, or I pretend not to hear, (b) I refuse to hear; I disobey, disregard.
παρακούω.sd: to mishear, i.e. (by implication) to disobey
παρακούω.as:
παρ-ακούω,
[in LXX: Es 3:3, 8 (עבר, עשׂה, c. neg.) 4:147:4 (חרשׁ hi.), Is 65:12 (שׁמע, c. neg.), I Es 4:11, To 3:4*;]
1.to overhear.
2.to hear amiss or imperfectly.
3. Later (as in LXX, Polyb., Plut.; also in π., v. MM, xviii), to hear without heeding, take no heed: Mk 5:36; c. gen., Mt 18:17.†

παλιγγενεσία.sd: (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), i.e. (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration

παραχρῆμα.sd: at the thing itself, i.e. instantly
παραχρῆμα.der: from G3844 (παρά) and G5536 (χρῆμα) (in its original sense);
παραχρῆμα.as:
παραχρῆμα,
adv.
(= παρὰ τὸ χρῆμα), [in LXX: Nu 6:912:4, Is 29:530:13 (פִּתְאֹם), etc.;]
on the spot, forthwith, instantly: Mt 21:19, 20, Lk 1:644:395:258:44, 47, 5513:1318:4319:1122:60, Ac 3:75:1012:2313:1116:26, 33 (on the usage in Mt, Lk, v. Dalman, Words, 28 f.).†

παγιδεύω.as:
† παγιδεύω
(< παγίς), [in LXX: I Ki 28:9 (נקשׁ hith.), Ec 9:12 (יקשׁ pu.)*;]
to ensnare: metaph., c. acc., ἐν λόγῳ, Mt 22:15 (not elsewhere).†

παροψίς.long: prop: a dainty side-dish; meton: a plate, dish, platter.
παροψίς.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G3795 (ὀψάριον);
παροψίς.as:
* παρ-οψίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(< παρά, ὄψον; v.s. ὀψάριον),
1.a side-dish of dainties (Xen., al.).
2. In Comic poets and late prose, the dish itself on which the dainties are served: Mt 23:25, 26 (In this sense it is condemned by the Atticists; v. Rutherford, NPhr., 265 f.)†

παρουσία.long: (a) presence, (b) a coming, an arrival, advent, especially of the second coming of Christ.
παρουσία.sd: a being near, i.e. advent (often, return; specially, of Christ to punish Jerusalem, or finally the wicked); (by implication) physically, aspect
παρουσία.der: from the present participle of G3918 (πάρειμι);
παρουσία.as:
παρ-ουσία, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ne 2:6 A, Jth 10:18, II Mac 8:1215:21, III Mac 3:17*;]
1. usually in cl., a being present, presence: I Co 16:17, II Co 10:10; opp. to ἀπουσία, Phl 2:12 (cf. II Mac 15:21).
2.a coming, arrival, advent (Soph., Eur., Thuc., al., v. LS, s.v.; so Jth 10:18, II Mac 8:12): II Co 7:6, 7, Phl 1:26, II Th 2:9; in late writers (v. M, Th., 145 ff.; MM, xix; LAE, 372 ff.) as technical term for the visit of a king; hence, in NT, specif. of the Advent or Parousia of Christ: Mt 24:3, 27, 37, 39, I Co 15:23, I Th 2:193:134:155:23, II Th 2:1, 8, Ja 5:7, 8, II Pe 1:163:4, 12, I Jo 2:28.†

πάσχα.g: the feast of Passover, the Passover lamb
πάσχα.long: the feast of Passover, the Passover lamb.
πάσχα.sd: the Passover (the meal, the day, the festival or the special sacrifices connected with it)
πάσχα.as:
† πάσχα, τό, indecl. (Aram. טַּסְחָא),
[in LXX for פֶּסַח;]
1. the festival of the Passover: Mt 26:2, Mk 14:1, Lk 22:1, Jo 2:13, 236:411:5512:118:3919:14, Ac 12:4, He 11:28; .ἡ ἐορτὴ τοῦ π., Lk 2:41, Jo 13:1.
2. By meton.,
(a)the paschal supper: ἑτοιμάζειν τὸ π., Mt 26:19, Mk 14:16, Lk 22:8, 13; ποιεῖν τό π., Mt 26:18;
(b)the pasohal lamb: θύειν τό π. (Ex 12:21), Mk 14:12, Lk 22:7; of Christ, I Co 5:7; φαγεῖν τὸ π. (lamb or supper), Mt 26:17, Mk 14:12, 14, Lk 22:11, 15, Jo 18:28 (cf. II Ch 30:17).†

παρέχω.long: act. and mid: I offer, provide, confer, afford, give, bring, show, cause.
παρέχω.sd: to hold near, i.e. present, afford, exhibit, furnish occasion
παρέχω.kj: bring, do, give, keep, minister, offer, shew, + trouble
παρέχω.as:
παρ-έχω,
[in LXX: Ps 29 (30):7 (עמד hi.), etc.;]
I. Act.,
1.to furnish, provide, supply; with ref. to incorporeal things, to afford, show, give, cause: c. acc., Ac 22:2, I Ti 1:4; c. acc. et dat., Mt 26:10, Mk 14:6, Lk 11:718:5, Ac 16:1617:3128:2, Ga 6:17, I Ti 6:17.
2.to present, offer: c. acc. et dat., Lk 6:29; c. prop. reflex. et acc. pred., to show or present oneself (v. infr., and cf. Bl., § 55, 1).
II. Mid.,
1.to supply, furnish or display of one's own part: c. acc. et dat., Lk 7:4, Ac 19:24, Col 4:1.
2. In late writers, c. prop. reflex. et acc. pred. (= act. ut supr.), to show or present oneself (Xen., FlJ, al.; cf. M, Pr., 248; Deiss., BS, 254): Tit 2:7.†

πάντοτε.sd: every when, i.e. at all times
πάντοτε.as:
** πάντοτε,
adv. of time
(< πᾶς), [in LXX: Wi 11:2119:18*;] in late writers (once in Arist.) for διαπαντός, ἑκάστοτε,
at all times, always: Mt 26:11, Mk 14:7, Lk 15:31, Jo 6:34, Ro 1:10, and freq. in Paul. Epp.

πατάσσω.long: I smite, strike (as with a sword), smite to death, afflict.
πατάσσω.sd: to knock (gently or with a weapon or fatally)
πατάσσω.as:
πατάσσω,
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for נכה hi., also for נגף, etc.;]
1. in Hom., intrans., to beat (of the heart).
2. Trans. = πλήσσω, to strike, smite: absol., ἐν μαχαίρᾳ, Lk 22:49; c. acc. pers., Mt 26:51, Lk 22:50; c. acc. rei, Ac 12:7; of a deadly blow, Mt 26:31, Mk 14:27, Ac 7:24. Metaph., of disease: Ac 12:23, Re 11:619:15.†

πάρειμι.long: I am present, am near; I have come, arrived.
πάρειμι.sd: to be near, i.e. at hand; neuter present participle (singular) time being, or (plural) property
πάρειμι.kj: come, X have, be here, + lack, (be here) present
πάρειμι.der: from G3844 (παρά) and G1510 (εἰμί) (including its various forms);
πάρειμι.as:
πάρ-ειμι,
[in LXX for בּוֹא, etc.;]
1.to be by, at hand or present;
(a) of persons: Re 17:8; παρών (opp. to ἀπών), I Co 5:3, II Co 10:2, 1113:2, 10; seq. ἐπί, c. gen., Ac 24:19; ἐνώπιον, Ac 10:33; ἐνθάδε, Ac 17:6; πρός, c. acc. pers., Ac 12:20, II Co 11:8, Ga 4:18, 20;
(b) of things: of time, ὁ καιρός, Jo 7:6; τ. παρόν, He 12:11; ἡ ἀλήθεια, II Pe 1:12; ταῦτα, II Pe 1:9; τ. παρόντα, He 13:5.
2.to have come or arrived (Hdt., Thuc., al.; v. Field, Notes, 65): Lk 13:1, Jo 11:28, Ac 10:21; seq. εἰς, Col 1:6; seq. ἐπί, c. acc. rei, Mt 26:50 (cf. συν-πάρειμι).†

παρίστημι.g: I bring, present, come up to and stand by
παρίστημι.long: I bring, present, prove, come up to and stand by, am present.
παρίστημι.sd: to stand beside, i.e. (transitively) to exhibit, proffer, (specially), recommend, (figuratively) substantiate; or (intransitively) to be at hand (or ready), aid
παρίστημι.kj: assist, bring before, command, commend, give presently, present, prove, provide, shew, stand (before, by, here, up, with), yield
παρίστημι.as:
παρ-ίστημι,
[in LXX for עמד, etc.;]
I. Trans. verb. in pres., impf., fut., 1 aor.;
1.to place beside, present, provide: c. acc., Ac 9:4123:24, II Co 4:14, Col 1:28; c. acc. et dat., Mt 26:53, Lk 2:22, Ac 1:323:33, I Co 8:8; seq. acc. pred., Ro 6:13, 16 (late pres., παριστάνετε), Ro 6:1912:1, II Co 11:2, Eph 5:27, Col 1:22, II Ti 2:15.
2.to present to the mind (cl.): by argument, to prove (Xen., FlJ, al.), c. acc., Ac 24:13.
II. Intrans. in pf., plpf., 2 aor.;
1.to stand by or beside one: c. dat. pers., Ac 1:109:3923:227:23; ptcp., Mk 14:47, 69, 7015:35, 39, Jo 18:2219:26.
2.to appear: c. nom. pred., seq. ἐνώπιον, Ac 4:10; c. dat. pers., Ac 27:24; so fut. mid. (of. LS, s.v., B, ii, 2), Ro 14:10.
3.to be at hand, be present, have come: Ac 4:26(LXX); of servants in attendance, ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ, Lk 1:19; absol., οἱ παρεστῶτες, Lk 19:24; seq. αὐτῷ, Ac 23:2, 4; of time, Mk 4:29.
4.to stand by for help or defence (Hom., Dem., Xen., al.): c. dat. pers., Ro 16:2, II Ti 4:17.†

παίω.sd: to hit (as if by a single blow and less violently than G5180 (τύπτω)); specially, to sting (as a scorpion)
παίω.as:
παίω,
[in LXX chiefly for נכה hi.;]
to strike, smite: with the hand or fist, Mt 26:68, Lk 22:64; with a sword, Mk 14:47, Jo 18:10; of a reptile, to sting: Re 9:5.†

παιδίσκη.long: a female slave, maidservant, maid, young girl.
παιδίσκη.sd: a girl, i.e. (specially), a female slave or servant
παιδίσκη.as:
παιδίσκη, -ης, ἡ,
dimin, of παῖς, [in LXX for שִׁפְחָה, אָמָה, etc.;]
1.a young girl, a maiden (נַעֲרָה, Ru 4:12).
2. Colloq., a young female slave, a maid-servant (v. Kennedy, Sources, 40 f.; Deiss., LAE, 186, 3322): Mt 26:69, Mk 14:66, 69, Lk 12:4522:56, Jo 18:17, Ac 12:1316:16; of Hagar, Ga 4:22, 23, 30(LXX); id., metaph., Ga 4:31.†
SYN.: v.s. παῖς.

παραπορεύομαι.long: I go past, pass by, pass along by.
παραπορεύομαι.as:
παρα-πορεύομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for עבר;]
1.to go beside, accompany.
2.to go past, pass by: Mt 27:39, Mk 11:2015:29; seq. διά, c. gen., Mk 2:239:30 (WH, mg.).†

παρασκευή.long: the day of preparation, the day before the Sabbath, Friday.
παρασκευή.as:
παρα-σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ex 35:2439:22 (42) (עֲבֹדָה, with v.l., ἀποσκ-, κατασκ-), Jth 2:174:5, I Mac 9:35א, II Mac 15:21*;]
1.preparation.
2.equipment (Jth 2:174:5).
3. In Jewish usage, the day of preparation for a Sabbath or a feast (= προσάββατον, q.v.): Mt 27:62, Mk 15:42, Lk 23:54, Jo 19:31; c. gen., τοῦ πάσχα, Jo 19:14; τ. Ἰουδαίων, Jo 19:42 (it is the name for Friday in MGr.).†

πανταχοῦ.der: genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of G3956 (πᾶς);
πανταχοῦ.as:
πανταχοῦ,
adv.,
[in LXX: Is 42:22 (כֻּלָּם)*;]
everywhere: Mk 1:2816:20, Lk 9:6, Ac 17:3024:328:22, I Co 4:17.†

πάντοθεν.long: from all sides, on all sides.
πάντοθεν.as:
πάντοθεν,
adv.
(< πᾶς), [in LXX: Je 31 (48):31 (כֻּלֹּה), al.;]
from all sides: Mk 1:45, Lk 19:43, He 9:4.†

παρατηρέω.sd: to inspect alongside, i.e. note insidiously or scrupulously
παρατηρέω.as:
παρα-τηρέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Ps 36 (37):12 (זמם), 129 (130):8 (שׁמר), Da TH 6:11 (12), Su 1:12, 15, 16*;]
1.to watch closely, observe narrowly: so mid., τ. πύλας, Ac 9:24; with evil intent, Mk 3:2, Lk 20:20 (absol., v. Field, Notes, 74); so mid., Lk 6:714:1.
2.to observe scrupulously (of days and seasons; cf. Ex 12:42, Sm.): mid., Ga 4:10.†

παραδέχομαι.sd: to accept near, i.e. admit or (by implication) delight in
παραδέχομαι.as:
παρα-δέχομαι,
[in LXX: Ex 23:1 (נשׂא), Pr 3:12 (רצה), II Mac 4:22 R, III Mac 7:12*;]
to receive, admit;
(a) of things: Mk 4:20, Ac 15:416:2122:18, I Ti 5:19;
(b) of persons: He 12:6(LXX).†

παρόμοιος.as:
* παρ-όμοιος, -ον
(also -η (Hdt.), -α (Arist.), -ον),
much like, like: Mk 7:13.†

παρρησία.long: freedom, openness, especially in speech; boldness, confidence.
παρρησία.sd: all out-spokenness, i.e. frankness, bluntness, publicity; by implication, assurance
παρρησία.kj: bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly(-ness)
παρρησία.der: from G3956 (πᾶς) and a derivative of G4483 (ῥέω);
παρρησία.as:
παρρησία, -ας, ἡ
(< πᾶς + ῥῆσις, speech), [in LXX: Le 26:13 (μετὰ π., קוֹמְמִיּוּת), Pr 1:2010:10, Wi 5:1, al.;]
1.freedom of speech, plainness, openness, freedom in speaking (Eur., Plat., al.): Ac 4:13, II Co 3:12; παρρησίᾳ, adverbially, freely, openly, plainly, Mk 8:32, Jo 7:13, 2610:2411:1416:2918:20; opp. to ἐν παροιμίαις, Jo 16:25; ἐν π., Eph 6:19; μετὰ π., Ac 2:294:29, 3128:31.
2. In LXX (I Mac 4:18, Wi 5:1, al.), FlJ, and NT, also (from the absence of fear which accompanies freedom of speech), confidence, boldness: II Co 7:4, Phl 1:20, I Ti 3:13; ἔχειν π., Eph 3:12, Phm 8, He 3:610:19, 35, I Jo 2:283:214:175:14; μετὰ π., He 4:16; ἐν π., Col 2:15; id. (as בפרהסיא in Rabbinic lit.; v. Westc., Jo., i, 262), in public, Jo 7:4 and (without ἐν) 11:54.†

παιδιόθεν.as:
παιδιόθεν
(< παιδίον),
adv.,
[in LXX: Ge 47:3*;]
= cl. ἐκ παιδός, παιδίου, from childhood: Mk 9:21.†

παραφέρω.g: I turn aside, carry away, remove
παραφέρω.long: I turn aside, carry away, remove, cause to pass away; pass: I am misled, seduced.
παραφέρω.sd: to bear along or aside, i.e. carry off (literally or figuratively); by implication, to avert
παραφέρω.der: from G3844 (παρά) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate forms);
παραφέρω.as:
παρα-φέρω,
[in LXX: I Ki 21:13 (14) (הלל hithpo.), and as v.l.2*;]
1.to bring to, set before, esp. of food (Hdt., al.).
2.to take or carry away: c. acc. rei, seq. ἀπό, Mk 14:36, Lk 22:42; pass., seq. ὑπό, Ju 12; metaph., pass., c. dat., He 13:9.†

παραιτέομαι.long: I beg off, make excuse, deprecate, refuse, reject, decline, shun, avoid.
παραιτέομαι.sd: to beg off, i.e. deprecate, decline, shun
παραιτέομαι.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G154 (αἰτέω);
παραιτέομαι.as:
παρ-αιτέομαι, -οῦμαι,
[in LXX for בּקשׁ pi., etc.;]
1.to beg of or from another: Mk 15:6 (Rec. ὅνπερ ᾐτοῦντο, v. Field, Notes, 43).
2.to deprecate;
(a) prop., c. neg., to entreat that not (Thuc., al.): He 12:19;
(b)to refuse, decline, avoid: o. acc., I Ti 4:75:11, II Ti 2:23, Tit 3:10, He 12:25 (EV; but v. Field, Notes, 234).
3.to beg off, ask to be excused, excuse (Polyb., al.) : Lk 14:18, 19 (He 12:25, Field, Notes, 234).†

παρακολουθέω.long: I accompany, follow closely, characterize, both lit. and met.; I investigate.
παρακολουθέω.sd: to follow near, i.e. (figuratively) attend (as a result), trace out, conform to
παρακολουθέω.kj: attain, follow, fully know, have understanding
παρακολουθέω.as:
** παρ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: II Mac 8:119:27 R*;]
c. dat., to follow closely, accompany. Metaph., in various senses,
(a)to result: Mk 16:[17];
(b)to follow up, trace, investigate: Lk 1:3 (so freq. in cl.);
(c)to follow as a standard of conduct: I Ti 4:6, II Ti 3:10. (For exx. from π., v. MM, xviii.)†

πατριά.sd: paternal descent, i.e. (concretely) a group of families or a whole race (nation)
πατριά.der: as if feminine of a derivative of G3962 (πατήρ);
πατριά.as:
πατριά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< πατήρ), [in LXX chiefly for אָב, Ex 6:14, al., also for מִשְׁפָּחָה, Ex 6:15, II Ki 14:7, Ps 21 (22):27, al.;]
1.lineage, ancestry (Hdt.).
2. = πάτρα (more common in cl.), a family or tribe (so sometimes in Hdt., in LXX of related people, in a sense narrower than φυλή and wider than οἶκος; v. Ex 12:3, Nu 32:28): Lk 2:4; in a wider sense (I Ch 16:28, Ps 21 (22):27), Ac 3:25(LXX), Eph 3:15.†

παράκλησις.long: a calling for, summons, hence: (a) exhortation, (b) entreaty, (c) encouragement, joy, gladness, (d) consolation, comfort.
παράκλησις.as:
παρά-κλησις, -εως, ἡ
(< παρακαλέω), [in LXX: Jb 21:2, Ps 93 (94):19, Ho 13:14, Na 3:7, Is 57:1866:11, Je 16:7 (נחם, its parts and derivatives), Je 38 (31):9 (תַּחֲנוּן), Is 28:2930:7, I Mac 10:2412:9, II Mac 7:2415:11*;]
1.a calling to one's aid, summons (Thus.), hence, appeal, entreaty (Strab., Plut., al., I Mac 10:24; cf. Lft., Notes, 20): II Co 8:4.
2.exhortation, encouragement: Ac 15:31, Ro 12:8, I Co 14:3, II Co 8:17, Phl 2:1, I Th 2:3, I Ti 4:13, He 12:5; λόγος (τῆς) π., Ac 13:15, He 13:22; υἱὸς π., Ac 4:36.
3.consolation, comfort (Phalar., LXX): Lk 6:24, Ac 9:31, II Co 1:4-77:4, 7, 13, II Th 2:16, Phm 7; τ. γραφῶν, Ro 15:4; θεὸς τῆς π., Ro 15:5, II Co 1:3; π. τοῦ Ἰσραήλ (v. Dalman, Words, 109 f.), Lk 2:25.†

παρθενία.as:
παρθενία, -ας, ἡ
(< παρθένος), [in LXX: Je 3:4 (נְעוּרִים), Si 15:242:10, IV Mac 18:8*;]
virginity: Lk 2:36.†

πάντως.long: wholly, entirely, in every way, by all means, certainly.
πάντως.sd: entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event
πάντως.kj: by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely
πάντως.as:
πάντως,
adv.
(< πάς), [in LXX: IV Ki 5:11 (v. Thackeray, Gr., 47), To 14:8, al.;]
altogether, by all means;
(a) without neg. (from Hdt. on): I Co 16:12; esp. in strong affirmations, surely, at all events: Lk 4:23, Ac 21:2228:4, I Co 9:10;
(b) c. neg. (so always in Hom.), in a complete negation: Ro 3:9; in a partial negation (Bl., § 75, 7), I Co 5:10.†

παύω.long: (a) act: I cause to cease, restrain, hinder, (b) mid: I cease, stop, leave off.
παύω.sd: to stop (transitively or intransitively), i.e. restrain, quit, desist, come to an end
παύω.as:
παύω,
[in LXX for כּלה pi., etc.;]
to make to cease, restrain, hinder: c. acc. rei, seq. ἀπό, I Pe 3:10(LXX). Mid., to cease, leave off: Lk 8:2411:1, Ac 20:1, I Co 13:8; c. ptcp., Lk 5:4, Ac 5:426:1313:1020:3121:32, Eph 1:16, Col 1:9, He 10:2; c. gen., ἀμαρτίας, I Pe 4:1 (WH, mg., R, txt.); c. dat., I Pe 4:1 (WH, txt., R, mg.).†

παραλύομαι.sd: to loosen beside, i.e. relax (perfect passive participle, paralyzed or enfeebled)
παραλύομαι.kj: feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy
παραλύομαι.as:
παρα-λύω,
[in LXX: Je 6:24, 27:43, Ez 21:7 (12) (רפה), etc.;]
1.to loose from the side, set free.
2.to weaken, enfeeble; pass., to be enfeebled, esp. by a paralytic stroke: Lk 5:18, 24, Ac 8:79:33, He 12:12(LXX).†

παράδοξος.der: from G3844 (παρά) and G1391 (δόξα) (in the sense of seeming);
παράδοξος.as:
** παράδοξος, -ον
(< παρά, δόξα), [in LXX: Jth 13:13, Wi 5:216:1719:5, Si 43:25; II-IV Mac3*;]
contrary to received opinion, incredible, marvellous: pl., Lk 5:26.†
SYN.: v.s. δύναμις.

παράλιος.long: adjacent to the sea, on the coast.
παράλιος.as:
παρ-άλιος, -ον
(in cl., chiefly -α, -ον), [in LXX for יָם, הַיָּם, חוֹף, etc., c. prep.;]
by the sea; ἡ π. (sc. χώρα, in LXX ἡ παραλία, De 1:7, Jos 9:1, Jth 1:7, al.), the sea coast: Lk 6:17.†

παρακαλύπτομαι.as:
παρα-καλύπτω,
[in LXX: Is 44:8 (פּחד), Ez 22:26 (עלם hi.)*;]
to cover by hanging something beside, to hide: metaph. (as Plat., al.), Lk 9:45.†

πατέω.der: from a derivative probably of G3817 (παίω) (meaning a "path");
πατέω.as:
πατέω, -ῶ,,
[in LXX for דּרךְ, etc.;]
1. intrans., to tread, walk: seq. ἐπάνω ὄφεων κ.τ.λ. (fig.), Lk 10:19 (cf. Ps 90 (91):13).
2. Trans., to tread on, trample: τ. ληνόν, Re 14:2019:15 (cf. Jg 9:27, La 1:15, al.); of the desecration of Jerusalem by its enemies, Lk 21:24, Re 11:2 (cf. κατα-, περι-, ἐν-περι-πατέω).†

πανδοχεῖον.sd: all-receptive, i.e. a public lodging-place (caravanserai or khan)
πανδοχεῖον.der: neuter of a presumed compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and a derivative of G1209 (δέχομαι);
πανδοχεῖον.as:
* παν-δοχεῖον (-δοκίον, T), -ου, τό
(< πανδοχεύς), late form of Att. πανδοκεῖον,
an inn (khân, caravanserai): Lk 10:34.†

πανδοχεύς.as:
* παν-δοχεύς, -έως, ὁ
(< πᾶς, δέχομαι), late form of the Att. πανδοκεύς (T, in l.),
an innkeeper, host: Lk 10:35.†

παρακαθέζομαι.as:
*† παρα-καθέζομαι,
to sit down beside: seq. πρός, Lk 10:39 (Plut.).†

πανοπλία.der: from a compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and G3696 (ὅπλον);
πανοπλία.as:
πανοπλία, -ας, ἡ
(< πᾶς, ὅπλον), [in LXX: II Ki 2:21 (חֲלִיצָה), Jb 39:20, Jth 14:3, Wi 5:17, Si 46:6, I, II, IV Mac6*;]
full armour: Lk 11:22; metaph. (cf. Wi 5:17), τ. θεοῦ, Eph 6:11, 13.†

παλαιόω.long: I make old, declare obsolete; pass: I grow old, become obsolete.
παλαιόω.sd: to make (passively, become) worn out, or declare obsolete
παλαιόω.as:
παλαιόω, -ῶ
(< παλαιός), [in LXX chiefly for בּלה, pi., in pass. for בּ׳ qal.;]
to make or declare old: He 8:13; pass., to become old: of things worn out by time and use (cf. Jo 9:13, Is 50:9, al., and v.s. παλαιός), Lk 12:33, He 1:11(LXX); τὸ παλαιούμενον, He 8:13 (where this and the act., v. supr., may have the sense of abrogate, v. LS, Zorell, s.v.).†
SYN.: γηράσκω.

παντελής.long: complete, entire, perfect, through all time.
παντελής.sd: full-ended, i.e. entire (neuter as noun, completion)
παντελής.as:
** παντελής, -ές
(< πᾶς, τέλος), [in LXX: III Mac 7:16 A*;]
all-complete, entire, perfect; εἰς τ. παντελές, completely, utterly: Lk 13:11, He 7:25 (where perhaps in temp. sense, finally; v. MM, xviii).†

παρατήρησις.as:
**† παρα-τήρησις, -εως, ἡ,
[in Aq.: Ex 12:42 (v.s. παρατηρέω)*;]
observation: Lk 17:20 (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

παρεμβάλλω.as:
παρ-εμ-βάλλω,
[in LXX freq. and chiefly for חנה;]
1.to put in beside or between, interpose.
2. In late writers (Polyb., al., LXX) as technical military term;
(a) of soldiers, to draw up in line (freq. in I Mac 2:32, al.);
(b) of siege works, to cast up: c. acc. et dat., χάρακά σοι, Lk 19:43.†

πανουργία.sd: adroitness, i.e. (in a bad sense) trickery or sophistry
πανουργία.as:
πανουργία, -ας, ἡ
(< πανοῦργος), [in LXX: Jos 9:4, Pr 1:48:5 (עׇרְמָה), Nu 24:22, Si 19:2521:2231 (34):10 (in all cases in good or indifferent sense)*;]
cleverness, in cl. nearly always in bad sense, craftiness, cunning, knavery: Lk 20:23, I Co 3:19 (LXX, φρόνησις, for עׇרְמָה) II Co 4:211:3, Eph 4:14.†

παγίς.long: a snare, trap (especially for catching birds) hence, met: stratagem, device, wile.
παγίς.sd: a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively, a trick or statagem (temptation)
παγίς.as:
παγίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(< πήγνυμι), [in LXX for פַּח, מוֹקֵשׁ, רֶשֶׁת, etc.;]
poët. (Aristoph., al.) and late for πάγη, a trap, snare; metaph. (as also in cl.): Lk 21:35, Ro 11:9(LXX), I Ti 3:76:9, II Ti 2:26.†

παιδεύω.long: (a) I discipline, educate, train, (b) more severely: I chastise.
παιδεύω.sd: to train up a child, i.e. educate, or (by implication), discipline (by punishment)
παιδεύω.as:
παιδεύω
(< παίς), [in LXX chiefly for יסר;]
1. as in cl., to train children, hence, generally, to teach, instruct: Ac 7:2222:3, I Ti 1:20, Tit 2:12.
2. As in LXX (Ps 6:2, Pr 19:18, Wi 3:5, al., and for prob. ex. from π., v. MM, xviii), to chasten, correct, chastise: Lk 23:16, 22, II Ti 2:25, He 12:7, 10; of divine chastening, I Co 11:32, II Co 6:9, He 12:6, Re 3:19.†
SYN.: διδάσκω, q.v.

παμπληθεί.sd: in full multitude, i.e. concertedly or simultaneously
παμπληθεί.der: dative case (adverb) of a compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and G4128 (πλῆθος);

παράδεισος.sd: a park, i.e. (specially), an Eden (place of future happiness, "paradise")
παράδεισος.as:
παράδεισος, -ου, ὁ
(an Oriental word, first used by Xen. of the parks of Persian kings and nobles), [in LXX chiefly for גַּן, Ge 1:8 ff., al.; also for עֵדֶן, Is 51:3; פַּרְדֵּס, Ne 2:8, Ec 2:5;]
1.a park, pleasure-ground, garden (LXX), an orchard (in π., v. MM, ii, xviii; Deiss., BS, 148).
2.Paradise, the abode of the blessed dead: Lk 23:43, II Co 12:4, Re 2:7.†

παρακύπτω.g: I stoop, peer in, look down
παρακύπτω.long: I stoop, peer in, look down, look intently.
παρακύπτω.sd: to bend beside, i.e. lean over (so as to peer within)
παρακύπτω.as:
παρα-κύπτω,
[in LXX chiefly for שׁקף ni., hi.;]
1.to stoop sideways.
2.to stoop to look: Lk 24:12 (R, txt.), Jo 20:5, 11. Metaph. (v. Hort, Ja., in l.), to look into: seq. εἰς, Ja 1:25, I Pe 1:12.†

παροικέω.long: I sojourn, dwell in as a stranger.
παροικέω.sd: to dwell near, i.e. reside as a foreigner
παροικέω.as:
παρ-οικέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for גּוּר, also for ישׁב, שׁכן;]
1 in cl., to dwell beside (c. acc.), among (c. dat.) or near by (absol.).
2 In late writers, to dwell in a place as aπάροικος (q.v.) or stranger: Lk 24:18, He 11:9.†

παραβιάζομαι.long: I urge, press, constrain by entreaties.
παραβιάζομαι.sd: to force contrary to (nature), i.e. compel (by entreaty)
παραβιάζομαι.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G971 (βιάζω);
παραβιάζομαι.as:
† παρα-βιάζομαι,
[in LXX: Ge 19:9, IV Ki 2:17 (בְּ׳פָּצַר), De 1:43 (זוּד hi.), I Ki 28:23 (בְּ׳פָּרַץ) v.1.4*;]
1. prop., to force against nature or law.
2.to compel by force (Polyb.).
3.to constrain by entreaty (Ge 19:9, I Ki 28:23): Lk 24:29, Ac 16:15.†

παιδάριον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3816 (παῖς);
παιδάριον.as:
παιδάριον, -ου, τό, dimin. of παῖς,
[in LXX chiefly for נַעַר;]
a little boy, a lad (in late and colloq. Gk. the word seems to be used with greater latitude and even to lose its dimin. force entirely; cf. To 6:2, 3, and v. MM, xviii): Jo 6:9.†
SYN.: v.s. παῖς.

παροιμία.long: a cryptic saying, an allegory; a proverb, figurative discourse.
παροιμία.sd: apparently a state alongside of supposition, i.e. (concretely) an adage; specially, an enigmatical or fictitious illustration
παροιμία.der: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and perhaps a derivative of G3633 (οἴομαι);
παροιμία.as:
παροιμία, -ας, ἡ
(< πάροιμος, by the way), [in LXX. Pr tit1:125:1, (מָשָׁל) subscr., Si 6:358:818:2939:347:17*;]
1.a wayside saying (Hesych.; v. LS, s.v.), a byword, maxim, proverb: II Pe 2:22.
2. In NT, of figurative discourse (as מָשָׁל, Is 14:4, al.), a parable, allegory: Jo 10:616:25, 29 (v. Abbott, Essays, 82 ff.).†
SYN.: παραβολή, q.v.

παραμυθέομαι.sd: to relate near, i.e. (by implication) encourage, console
παραμυθέομαι.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of a derivative of G3454 (μῦθος);
παραμυθέομαι.as:
** παρα-μυθέομαι, -οῦμαι,
[in LXX: II Mac 15:9 (Sm.8)*;]
1.to encourage, exhort.
2.to comfort, console: c. acc. pers., Jo 11:31, I Th 2:115:14; id. seq. περί, Jo 11:19.†
SYN.: παρακαλέω.

παράκλητος.long: (a) an advocate, intercessor, (b) a consoler, comforter, helper, (c) Paraclete.
παράκλητος.as:
** παρά-κλητος, -ον
(< παρακαλέω), [in Aq., Th.: Jb 16:2*;]
called to one's aid in a judicial cause (Dion. Cass.); hence, most freq. as subst., ὁ π., an advocate, pleader, intercessor (Dem., al.; so in Rabbinic lit., פְּרַקְלִיטָא), "a friend of the accused person, called to speak to his character, or otherwise enlist sympathy in his favour" (Field, Notes, 102). In NT, specif., ὁ π.,
(a) of Christ, I Jo 2:1 (v. ICC, Jo. Epp., 23 ff.);
(b) of the Holy Spirit (AV, comforter; but v. opp. c.), Jo 14:16, 2615:2616:7 (cf. also Abbott, Essays, 86, 97; Deiss., LAE, 339 f.; MM, xviii; Westc., Jo., ii, 188 ff.).

Πάρθος.long: a Parthian, an inhabitant of the country beyond the eastern boundary of the Roman Empire between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf.
Πάρθος.sd: a Parthian, i.e. inhabitant of Parthia

Παμφυλία.long: Pamphylia, a Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.
Παμφυλία.sd: every-tribal, i.e. heterogeneous (G5561 (χώρα) being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor
Παμφυλία.der: from a compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and G4443 (πυρά);
Παμφυλία.as:
Παμφυλία, -ας, ἡ,
Pamphylia, a province of Asia Minor: Ac 2:1013:1314:2415:3827:5.†

πατριάρχης.long: a patriarch, head or founder of a family.
πατριάρχης.as:
† πατριάρχης, -ου, ὁ
(< πατριά, ἄρχω), [in LXX: I Ch 24:31 (אָב), II Ch 19:826:12 (הָאָבוֹתרֹאשׁ), I Ch 27:12 (שַׂר), II Ch 23:20 (שַׂר־הַמֵּאוֹת), IV Mac 7:1916:25*;]
a patriarch: Ac 2:297:8, 9, He 7:4.†

παραγγελία.long: a command, charge, injunction; a precept, rule of living.
παραγγελία.as:
* παρ-αγγελία, -ας, ἡ
(< παραγγέλλω),
an instruction, charge, command: Ac 5:2816:24, I Th 4:2, I Ti 1:5, 18. (In Xen., Polyb., of a military order.)†

παραθεωρέω.as:
* παρα-θεωρέω, -ῶ,
1.to examine side by side, compare.
2.to overlook, neglect: pass., Ac 6:1.†

Παρμενᾶς.long: Parmenas, one of the original seven deacons at Jerusalem.
Παρμενᾶς.der: probably by contraction for (a derivative of a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G3306 (μένω));

πάροικος.long: foreign, alien, subst: a foreigner, sojourner.
πάροικος.sd: having a home near, i.e. (as noun) a by-dweller (alien resident)
πάροικος.as:
πάρ-οικος, -ον,
[in LXX chiefly for גֵּר, תּוֹשַׁב;]
1. in cl. Attic, dwelling near, neighbouring; as subst., a neighbour.
2. In late writers (LXX, Philo) and in Inscr. (Deiss., BS, 227 f.; Kennedy, Sources, 102), foreign, alien; as subst., an alien, a sojourner: Ac 7:6(LXX), 29; metaph., ξένοι καὶ π. (opp. to συμπολίτης), Eph 2:19; π. καὶ παρεπιδήμους (q.v.), I Pe 2:11 (v. Lft. on Clem. Rom., 1 Co., § 1).†

παρρησιάζομαι.long: I speak freely, boldly; I am confident.
παρρησιάζομαι.sd: to be frank in utterance, or confident in spirit and demeanor
παρρησιάζομαι.as:
παρρησιάζομαι
(< παρρησία), [in LXX: Jb 22:26 (ענג hithp.), Ps 11 (12):593 (94):1, Pr 20:9, Ca 8:10, Si 6:11*;]
to speak freely or boldly, be bold in speech: Ac 9:27, 2813:4614:318:2619:826:26, Eph 6:20, I Th 2:2.†

παρασκευάζω.long: I prepare; mid: I prepare, make preparations.
παρασκευάζω.sd: to furnish aside, i.e. get ready
παρασκευάζω.der: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G4632 (σκεῦος);
παρασκευάζω.as:
παρα-σκευάζω,
[in LXX: Je 27 (50):42 (ערךְ), etc.;]
to prepare, make ready: absol. (sc. τ. δεῖπνον, etc.; of. Hdt., ix, 82, II Mac 2:27), Ac 10:10; mid., to prepare, make preparations: I Co 14:8 (cf. Je 50:42); pass., II Co 9:2, 3.†

Πάφος.long: Paphos, a city at the western end of Cyprus.
Πάφος.as:
Πάφος, -ου, ἡ,
Paphos, a city in Cyprus: Ac 13:6, 13.†

Παῦλος.sd: (little; but remotely from a derivative of G3973 (παύω), meaning the same); Paulus, the name of a Roman and of an apostle
Παῦλος.as:
Παῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. Paulus),
1.Sergius Paulus: Ac 13:7.
2.the Apostle Paul (cf. Σαῦλος): Ac 13:9, and freq. throughout Ac., Ro 1:1, I Co 1:1, al., II Pe 3:15.

παροικία.long: a sojourning, a dwelling in a strange land.
παροικία.as:
† παρ-οικία, -ας, ἡ
(< παροικέω, q.v.), [in LXX: II Es 8:35 (גּוֹלָה), Ps 33 (34):454 (55):15118 (119):54119 (120):5, La 2:22 (מגוֹר; and cogn. forms), Hb 3:16, I Es 5:7, Jth 5:9, Wi 19:10, Si prol. 2616:841:544:6, III Mac 6:367:19*;]
a sojourning: Ac 13:17, I Pe 1:17.†

παροτρύνω.long: I stir up, incite, urge on.
παροτρύνω.sd: to urge along, i.e. stimulate (to hostility)
παροτρύνω.as:
* παρ-οτρύνω,
to urge on, stir up: c. acc. pers., Ac 13:50 (Pind., Hipp., and late writers).†

παροίχομαι.sd: to escape along, i.e. be gone
παροίχομαι.as:
* παρ-οίχομαι,
to have passed by; of time, to be gone by: ἐν τ. παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς, Ac 14:16.†

παρενοχλέω.long: I trouble, cause disturbance to, annoy, harass.
παρενοχλέω.as:
παρ-εν-οχλέω, -ῶ
(cf. ἐνοχλέω), [in LXX for לאה hi. (Mi 6:3), etc.;]
to annoy concerning a matter (παρά): c. dat. pers., Ac 15:19.†

παροξυσμός.as:
παροξυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< παροξύνω), [in LXX: De 29:(28)27, Je 39 (32):37 (קֶצֶף)*;]
1.stimulation, provocation: π. ἀγάπης, He 10:14.
2.irritation: Ac 15:39.†

πανοικεί.g: with one's whole household or family
πανοικεί.long: with one's whole household or family.
πανοικεί.as:
πανοικεί (Rec., LTr., -κί),
adv.
(< πᾶς, οἶκος), a word rejected by strict Atticists, though found once in Plat. (Eryx., 392 c); [in LXX: Ex 1:1 (בַּיִת), III Mac 3:27 (where A in each case reads -κίᾳ, the Attic form, cf. Ge 50:8, al.)*;]
with all the household: Ac 16:34.†

παροξύνομαι.sd: to sharpen alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate
παροξύνομαι.der: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G3691 (ὀξύς);
παροξύνομαι.as:
παρ-οξύνω,
[in LXX for נאץ, קצף, רגז, etc.;]
1. primarily, but never so in cl., to sharpen (μάχαιραν, De 32:41, שׁנן).
2. Metaph., as always in cl.,
(a)to spur on, stimulate (Arist., Xen., al.);
(b)to provoke, rouse to anger (De 9:7, 18, Ps 105 (106):29, al.): pass., Ac 17:16, I Co 13:5.†

παρατυγχάνω.long: I come by chance, chance to meet.
παρατυγχάνω.sd: to chance near, i.e. fall in with
παρατυγχάνω.as:
* παρα-τυγχάνω,
to happen to be near or present: Ac 17:17.†

Πάγος.g: hill, crag (in Ἄρειος Πάγος, the Areopagus)

παρατείνω.sd: to extend along, i.e. prolong (in point of time)
παρατείνω.as:
παρα-τείνω,
[in LXX: Nu 23:28 (שׁקף ni.), etc.;]
to extend, prolong: τ. λόγον, Ac 20:7.†

παραβάλλω.sd: to throw alongside, i.e. (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken
παραβάλλω.as:
παρα-βάλλω,
[in LXX: Pr 2:24:205:1, 1322:17 (נטה hi.), Ru 2:16 (שׁלל), II Mac 14:38 (elsewhere as v.l.4)*;]
1.to throw to or beside, as fodder to horses (Hom., al.).
2.to lay beside, compare (Hdt., Plat., al.): Mk 4:30, Rec.
3. Reflexive, to betake oneself, come near; of seamen, to cross over: εἰς Σάμον, Ac 20:15.
4. In mid. = παρα-βολεύομαι, q.v.†

παραπλέω.as:
* παρα-πλέω,
to sail by or past: c. acc., Ac 20:16.†

Πάταρα.long: Patara, a town on the coast of the Roman province Lycia.
Πάταρα.sd: Patara, a place in Asia Minor
Πάταρα.as:
Πάταρα, -ων, τὰ,
Patara, a maritime city of Lycia: Ac 21:1.†

πανταχῇ.as:
πανταχῇ (Rec. -χῆ),
adv.,
[in LXX: Is 24:11 (בַּחוּצוֹת), Wi 2:9, II Mac 8:7*;]
everywhere: Ac 21:28.†

παρεμβολή.g: a camp, barracks, army in battle array
παρεμβολή.long: a camp, fort, castle, barracks, army in battle array.
παρεμβολή.sd: a throwing in beside (juxtaposition), i.e. (specially), battle-array, encampment or barracks (tower Antonia)
παρεμβολή.der: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G1685 (ἐμβάλλω);
παρεμβολή.as:
παρ-εμ-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< παρεμβάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲנֶה;]
1.an insertion, interpolation (Æschin.).
2. In the Macedonian dialect (Rutherford, NPhr., 473), as a military term;
(a)an army in battle array: He 11:34 (cf. Ex 14:19, 20, Jg 4:16, al.; freq. in Polyb.);
(b)a camp (Ex 29:14, al.): He 13:11, 13, Re 20:9;
(c)barracks, soldiers' quarters: Ac 21:34, 3722:2423:10, 16, 3228:16 (WH, txt., R, om.).†

πατρῷος.as:
πατρῷος, -α, -ον
(< πατήρ), [in LXX: Pr 27:10 (אָב), II Es 7:5, II-IV Mac12*;]
of one's fathers, received from one's fathers: Ac 22:324:1428:17.†

παρανομέω.sd: to be opposed to law, i.e. to transgress
παρανομέω.der: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G3551 (νόμος);
παρανομέω.as:
παρα-νομέω, ῶ,
[in LXX for חלל, etc., chiefly in Pss and II Mac;]
to be a παράνομος, to transgress the law: Ac 23:3.†

πάντῃ.as:
** πάντῃ (Rec. -τη),
adv.
(< πᾶς), [in LXX: Si 50:22, III Mac 4:1*;]
every way, entirely: Ac 24:3.†

παθητός.as:
* παθητός, -ή, -όν
(< πάσχω),
1.one who has suffered.
2.subject to suffering (R, mg., v. M, Pr., 222) or destined to suffer (AV, R, txt.): Ac 26:23.†

παραλέγομαι.sd: (specially), to lay one's course near, i.e. sail past
παραλέγομαι.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense);
παραλέγομαι.as:
* παρα-λέγω,
to lay beside; mid.,
(a)to lie beside (Hom.);
(b) later, of sailors, to sail past: c. acc., Ac 27:8, 13.†

παραινέω.sd: to mispraise, i.e. recommend or advise (a different course)
παραινέω.as:
** παρ-αινέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: II Mac 7:25, 26, III Mac 5:177:12*;]
toexhort, advise: c. acc. pers. et inf. (v. Bl., § 72, 5; M, Pr., 205), Ac 27:22; absol., seq. λέγων, Ac 27:9.†

παραχειμασία.as:
*† παρα-χειμασία, -ας, ἡ
(< παρα-χειμάζω),
a wintering: Ac 27:12 (Polyb., al.).†

παραχειμάζω.sd: to winter near, i.e. stay with over the rainy season
παραχειμάζω.as:
* παρα-χειμάζω,
to winter at a place: seq. εἰς, Ac 27:12; ἐν, Ac 28:11; πρὸς ὑμᾶς, I Co 16:6; ἐκεῖ, Tit 3:12.†

παράσημος.sd: side-marked, i.e. labelled (with a badge (figure-head) of a ship)
παράσημος.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);
παράσημος.as:
** παράσημος, -ον
(< σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: III Mac 2:29*;]
1. in cl., marked amiss, spurious, counterfeit. Later,
2.marked at the side, annotated (Plut.).
3.marked with a sign (LXX); as subst., a figurehead: Ac 28:11 (v. MM, xix).†

πάθος.sd: properly, suffering ("pathos"), i.e. (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence)
πάθος.as:
πάθος, -ους, τό
(< πάσχω), [in LXX: Jb 30:31 (אֵבֶל), Pr 25:20, and very freq. in IV Mac (1:1 ff., al.)*;] like πάθημα;
1.that which befalls one, that which one suffers.
2.a passive emotion or affection (esp. of violent emotion), a passion, passionate desire; in NT always in bad sense: Col 3:5; π. ἀτιμίας, Ro 1:26; π. ἐπιθυμίας, I Th 4:5.†
SYN.: π. = πάθημα, exc. that πάθημα is the more concrete and particular. In NT usage, π. represents the passive, ungoverned aspect of evil desire, as opp. to ἐπιθυμία, which is the active and also the more comprehensive term (v. Tr., Syn., lxxxvii); cf. also ὄρεξις.

παιδευτής.long: an instructor, trainer; almost: a chastiser.
παιδευτής.sd: a trainer, i.e. teacher or (by implication) discipliner
παιδευτής.as:
παιδευτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< παιδεύω), [in LXX: Ho 5:2 (מוּסָר), Si 37:19, IV Mac 5:349:6*;]
1. prop., a teacher, instructor: Ro 2:20.
2.a corrector, one who disciplines (cf. Ho 5:2): He 12:9.†

παράβασις.as:
παρά-βασις, -εως, ἡ
(< παραβαίνω), [in LXX: Ps 100 (101):3 (סֵטִים), IV Ki 2:24 A, Wi 14:31, II Mac 15:10*;]
1.a going aside, a deviation (Arist.).
2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaph., transgression (Plut., al.): Ro 4:155:14, He 2:29:15; τ. νόμου, Ro 2:23; ἐν π., I Ti 2:14; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, Ga 3:19.
SYN.: v.s. ἁμαρτία.

παραβάτης.as:
** παρα-βάτης, -ου, ὁ
(< παραβαίνω), [in Sm.: Ps 16 (17):4138 (139):19, Je 6:28*;]
1.one who stands beside, the warrior who stands by the charioteer (cf. παραβαίνω, 1).
2.a transgressor (Æsch., παρβάτης): Ga 2:18, Ja 2:9; π. νόμου, Ro 2:25, 27, Ja 2:11.†

πάρεσις.long: overlooking, suspension, remission of punishment for.
πάρεσις.as:
* πάρεσις, -εως, ἡ
(< παρίημι),
1.a letting go, dismissal.
2.prætermission, passing by (of debt or sin): Ro 3:25.†
SYN.: ἄφεσις, q.v.

παρακοή.as:
* παρ-ακοή, -ῆς, ἡ,
1.a hearing amiss (Plat.).
2. Later, as following inattention, disobedience: Ro 5:19, II Co 10:6, He 2:2 (cf. παρακούω, and v. Tr., Syn., § lxvi).†

παρεισέρχομαι.long: I enter secretly, come in from the side.
παρεισέρχομαι.sd: to come in alongside, i.e. supervene additionally or steathily
παρεισέρχομαι.as:
* παρ-εισ-έρχομαι,
1.to come in beside or by the way: Ro 5:20.
2.to come in secretly, steal in: Ga 2:4.†

πάθημα.long: (a) suffering, affliction, (b) passion, emotion, (c) an undergoing, an enduring.
πάθημα.sd: something undergone, i.e. hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence
πάθημα.der: from a presumed derivative of G3806 (πάθος);
πάθημα.as:
* πάθημα, -τος, τό
(< πάσχω), like πάθος,
1.that which befalls one, a suffering, affliction: pl., Ro 8:18, II Co 1:6, 7, Col 1:24, II Ti 3:11, He 2:1010:32, I Pe 5:9; of Christ's sufferings: τὰ εἰς Χ., I Pe 1:11; τ. Χριστσῦ, I Pe 5:1; id. as shared by Christians, II Co 1:5, Phl 3:10, I Pe 4:13.
2.a passive emotion, affection, passion: Ga 5:24; τ. ἁμαρτιῶν, Ro 7:5.
3. = τὸ πάσχειν, an enduring or suffering: c. gen. obj., He 2:9.†
SYN.: v.s. πάθος.

παράκειμαι.g: I am present with, rest with
παράκειμαι.long: I am at hand, am present with, rest with.
παράκειμαι.sd: to lie near, i.e. be at hand (figuratively, be prompt or easy)
παράκειμαι.as:
** παρά-κειμαι,
[in LXX: Jdt.3.2, 3, Si 30:1834 (31):16, Da LXX Bel 1:14, II, III Mac5*;]
to lie beside, be near, be present: Ro 7:18, 21.†

παραζηλόω.long: I make jealous, provoke to jealously, provoke to anger.
παραζηλόω.sd: to stimulate alongside, i.e. excite to rivalry
παραζηλόω.as:
† παρα-ζηλόω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: De 32:21, III Ki 14:22, Ps 77 (78):58 (קנא pi., hi.), Ps 36 (37):1, 7, 8 (חרה hith.), Si 30:3*;]
to provoke to jealousy: Ro 10:19(LXX)11:11, 14, I Co 10:22.†

παροργίζω.as:
παρ-οργίζω,
[in LXX chiefly for כּעס hi.;]
(in cl., passive only), to provoke to anger: Ro 10:19(LXX), Eph 6:4.†

Πατροβᾶς.der: perhaps a contraction for (a compound of G3962 (πατήρ) and G979 (βίος));

παιδαγωγός.long: a boy's guardian or tutor, a slave who had charge of the life and morals of the boys of a family, not strictly a teacher.
παιδαγωγός.sd: a boy-leader, i.e. a servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication, (figuratively) a tutor ("pædagogue"))
παιδαγωγός.der: from G3816 (παῖς) and a reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω);
παιδαγωγός.as:
* παιδαγωγός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< παῖς, ἄγω),
a guide, guardian, trainer of boys, a tutor (disting. from διδάσκαλος, Xen., Lac., 3, 1), usually a trusty slave: opp. to πατήρ, I Co 4:15; fig., of the Law, π. εἰς Χριστόν, Ga 3:24, 25.†

παρεδρεύω.as:
παρ-εδρεύω,
[in LXX: Pr 1:218:3*;]
to sit constantly beside, attend constantly (cf. MM, xix): τ. θυσιαστηρίῳ, I Co 9:13.†

παίζω.long: I play, sport (includes singing and dancing), play in the manner of children.
παίζω.as:
παίζω
(< παῖς), [in LXX: Ge 21:926:8, Ex 32:6 (צחק pi.); and more freq. (Jg 16:25, al.) for (שׁחק pi.;]
prop., to play as a child, hence, generally, to play (as with singing and dancing): I Co 10:7(LXX) (cf. ἐμ-παίζω).†

παραμυθία.as:
** παραμυθία, -ας, ἡ
(< παραμυθέομαι), [in LXX: Es 8:13, Wi 19:12*;]
1.encouragement, exhortation.
2.comfort, consolation: I Co 14:3.†
SYN.: παράκλησις.

παραμένω.long: I remain by, abide with; met: I persevere in.
παραμένω.sd: to stay near, i.e. remain (literally, tarry; or figuratively, be permanent, persevere)
παραμένω.as:
παρα-μένω,
[in LXX: Pr 12:7, Da TH 11:17 (עמד), etc.;]
to remain beside or near: He 7:23, Ja 1:25; of remaining alive, I Co 16:6 (WH, κατα-), Phl 1:25 (cf. συμ-παραμένω).†

πάροδος.as:
πάρ-οδος, -ου, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ge 38:14 (דֶּרֶךְ), etc.;]
a passing or passage: ἐν π., in passing, I Co 16:7.†

παραυτίκα.long: adv. with force of adj: present, immediate, for the moment.
παραυτίκα.sd: at the very instant, i.e. momentary
παραυτίκα.der: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G846 (αὐτός);
παραυτίκα.as:
παρ-αυτίκα,
adv.
(< πάραυτα = παρ’ αὐτά, sc. τὰ πράγματα), [in LXX: Ps 69 (70):3, To 4:14*;]
1.immediately.
2. C. subst., to express brief duration (cf. ἡ π. λαμπρότης, Thuc., ii, 64), momentary, for a moment: II Co 4:17.†

παντοκράτωρ.long: ruler of all, ruler of the universe, the almighty.
παντοκράτωρ.sd: the all-ruling, i.e. God (as absolute and universal sovereign)
παντοκράτωρ.as:
† παντοκράτωρ, -ορος, ὁ
(< πᾶς, κρατέω), [in LXX: freq. in Jb 5:8, 17, al. (שַׁדַּי), and for צְבָאוֹת, in the phrase θεός (κυρίος) π., II Ki 5:10, al., and freq. in Am, Za, Ma; also in Wi 7:25, Si 42:1750:14, 17, and freq. in Jth, II, III Mac;]
almighty: II Co 6:18, Re 1:84:811:1715:316:7, 1419:6, 1521:22.†

παραφρονέω.g: I am out of my senses
παραφρονέω.long: I am out of my senses, am beside myself.
παραφρονέω.as:
παρα-φρονέω
(< παρά, φρήν), [in LXX: Za 7:11 (סרר)*;]
to be beside oneself, be deranged: II Co 11:23.†

πανοῦργος.as:
πανοῦργος, -ον,
[in LXX chiefly for עָרוּם;]
ready to do anything;
(a) in cl., chiefly in bad sense, knavish, crafty: II Co 12:16;
(b) in good sense, skilful, clever (Pr 13:128:2).†

πατρικός.long: ancestral, paternal, belonging to the fathers (ancestors).
πατρικός.as:
πατρικός, -ή, -όν
(< πατήρ), [in LXX for אָב, Ge 50:8, al.;]
paternal, ancestral: Ga 1:14.†

παρείσακτος.as:
*† παρ-είσ-ακτος, -ον
(< παρεισάγω),
brought in secretly (as spies or traitors): Ga 2:4.†

παροργισμός.as:
† παρ-οργισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< παροργίζω), [in LXX: III Ki 15:30, IV Ki 23:26 (כַּעַס); IV Ki 19:3, Ne 9:18, 26 (נְאָצָה); Je 21:5 A (קֶצֶף)*;]
irritation ("distinguished from ὀργή as implying a less permanent state"; ICC, Eph., 140; and v. Tr., Syn., § xxxvii): Eph 4:26.†

παιδεία.long: discipline; training and education of children, hence: instruction; chastisement, correction.
παιδεία.sd: tutorage, i.e. education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction
παιδεία.as:
παιδεία (-ία, T), -ας, ἡ
(< παιδεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מוּסָר;]
1.the rearing of a child (Æsch.).
2.training, learning, instruction (Plat., al.): Eph 6:4, II Ti 3:16.
3. As in LXX (Pr 3:1115:5, al.), chastening, discipline: He 12:5(LXX), 7, 8, 11.†

πάλη.long: wrestling, a wrestling bout; hence: a struggle, fight, conflict, contest.
πάλη.as:
* πάλη, -ης, ἡ
(< πάλλω, to sway)
wrestling, hence, generally, fight, contest: fig., of the spiritual combat of Christians, Eph 6:12.†

παραμύθιον.long: comfort, consolation, an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement.
παραμύθιον.as:
** παραμύθιον, -ου, τό
(< παραμυθέομαι), [in LXX: Wi 3:18*;]
1.an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement: Phl 2:1 (cf. Plat., Legg., vi, 773 E, al.; v. Lft. and ICC, Phl 2:1).
2.assuagement, abatement, hence, consolation (Wi 3:18, and freq. in cl.).†

παραπλήσιον.der: neuter of a compound of G3844 (παρά) and the base of G4139 (πλησίον) (as adverb);
παραπλήσιον.as:
* παρα-πλήσιος, -α, -ον (Hdt., Plat., al.; also -ος, -ον, Thuc., Polyb.),
coming near, nearly resembling. Neut. -ον, adverbially, = ίως, in a way nearly resembling: c. dat., Phl 2:27.†

παραβολεύομαι.g: I expose myself to danger, am reckless
παραβολεύομαι.long: I expose myself to danger; I am adventuresome, reckless.
παραβολεύομαι.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G1011 (βουλεύω);
παραβολεύομαι.as:
*† παρα-βολεύομαι
= cl. παραβάλλομαι (II Mac 14:38),
to expose oneself to danger, hazard one's life: c. dat. ref., τ. ψυχῇ (v. M, Pr., 64), Phl 2:30 (Rec. παραβουλ-). Cited by Deiss., LAE, 84, 120.†

παραλογίζομαι.long: I deceive, beguile, reason falsely, mislead.
παραλογίζομαι.as:
παρα-λογίζομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for רמה pi.;]
1.to miscalculate.
2.to reason falsely, hence, to mislead: Col 2:4, Ja 1:22.†

παρηγορία.der: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά) (meaning to harangue an assembly);
παρηγορία.as:
** παρηγορία, -ας, ἡ
(< παρηγορέω, to address, exhort, console), [in LXX: IV Mac 5:126:1*;]
1.an address, exhortation (LXX, IV Mac 5:126:1).
2.comfort, consolation: Col 4:11.†

πατρολῴας.as:
* πατρολῴας (-αλῴας, Rec.; in cl. -αλοίας, v. Bl., § 3, 3; 6, 2, and cf. μητρολῴας), -ου, ὁ
(< πατήρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite),
(a)a parricide: I Ti 1:9 (AV, R, txt.);
(b)a smiter of his father: I Ti 1:9 (R, mg.).†

πάροινος.sd: staying near wine, i.e. tippling (a toper)
πάροινος.as:
*† πάρ-οινος, -ον,
= cl., παροινικός (παρά, οἶνος),
given to wine, drunken: I Ti 3:3, Tit 1:7.†

παραθήκη.long: a deposit, anything committed to one's charge or trust.
παραθήκη.as:
παρα-θήκη, -ης, ἡ
(< παρατίθημι), [in LXX: Le 6:2, 4 (5:21, 23) (פִּקָּדוֹן), and in To 10:13, II Mac 3:10, 15, v.l. for παρακαταθήκη (q.v.)*;]
a deposit or trust: I Ti 6:20, II Ti 1:12, 14 (for exx. of this form, v. MM, Exp., iii, xviii).†

παραρρέω.g: I am lost, perish, drift away
παραρρέω.long: (lit: I flow past, glide past, hence) I am lost, perish, or merely: I drift away (fall away) from duty.
παραρρέω.sd: to flow by, i.e. (figuratively) carelessly pass (miss)
παραρρέω.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the alternate of G4482 (ῥέω);
παραρρέω.as:
παρα-ρρέω,
[in LXX: Is 44:4 (יבל), Pr 3:21*;]
to flow by, drift away, slip away: He 2:1.†

παραπλησίως.sd: in a manner near by, i.e. (figuratively) similarly
παραπλησίως.der: adverb from the same as G3897 (παραπλήσιον);
παραπλησίως.as:
** παρα-πλησίως,
adv.
(< παραπλήσιος), [in Quint.: Ho 8:6*;]
in like manner: He 2:14.†

παραπικρασμός.as:
† παρα-πικρασμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< παραπικραίνω), [in LXX: Ps 94 (95):8 (מְרִיבָה elsewhere rendered Λοιδόρησις, Ex 17:7; ἀντιλογία, De 33:8, al.; λοιδορία, Nu 20:24)*;]
provocation: ἐν τῷ π. (Heb. at Meribah), He 3:8, 15(LXX).†

παραπικραίνω.sd: to embitter alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate
παραπικραίνω.as:
† παρα-πικραίνω,
[in LXX chiefly for מרה qal., hi., מְרִי, most freq. in Pss and Ez;]
to embitter, provoke: absol. (yet sc. τ. θεόν, cf. Ps 105 (106):7, Ez 2:5-8, al., and with τὸν θ. added, Ps 5:4, Ez 20:21, al.), He 3:16 (cf. παραπικρασμός).†

παραπίπτω.long: I fall away, fall back (into the unbelieving and godless ways of the old time).
παραπίπτω.sd: to fall aside, i.e. (figuratively) to apostatize
παραπίπτω.as:
παρα-πίπτω,
[in LXX: Ez 14:1315:818:2420:27 (מעל), 22:4 (אשׁם), Es 6:10 (נפל hi.), Wi 6:912:2, II Mac 10:4 A*;]
1. most freq. (Hdt., Thuc., al.), to fall in one's way, befall.
2.to fall into or in (seq. εἰς, Polyb.; c. dat., II Mac 10:4).
3.to fall away (Ez 14:1315:818:2420:2722:4, Wi 6:912:2; in Polyb., c. gen.): absol., He 6:6.
4.to fail (λόγος, Es 6:10; cf. I Ki 3:19).†

παραδειγματίζω.long: I put to open shame, make a public example of, put to disgrace.
παραδειγματίζω.sd: to show alongside (the public), i.e. expose to infamy
παραδειγματίζω.kj: make a public example, put to an open shame
παραδειγματίζω.as:
† παρα-δειγματίζω
(< δείκνυμι), [in LXX: Nu 25:4 (יקע hi.), Je 13:22 (חמס ni.), Ez 28:17 (רַאֲוָה), Es 4:17, Da LXX 2:5*;]
to set forth as an example; in bad sense, to put to open shame: He 6:6 (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

παρεπίδημος.g: residing in a strange country, a stranger
παρεπίδημος.long: residing in a strange country; subst: a stranger, sojourner.
παρεπίδημος.sd: an alien alongside, i.e. a resident foreigner
παρεπίδημος.der: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G1927 (ἐπιδημέω);
παρεπίδημος.as:
† παρ-επί-δημος, -ον
(v.s. ἐπιδημέω), [in LXX: Ge 23:4, Ps 38 (39):12 (תּוֹשָׁב)*;]
sojourning in a strange place; as subst., ὁ π., a sojourner: of Christians, I Pe 1:1; ξένοι καὶ π., He 11:13; πάροικοι καὶ π., I Pe 2:11 (v. Deiss., BS, 149).†

παρίημι.long: (a) I let pass, neglect, omit, disregard, (b) I slacken, loosen; pass: I am wearied.
παρίημι.as:
παρ-ίημι,
[in LXX: Je 4:31 (פּרשׂ pi.), etc.;]
1.to pass by or over, let alone, disregard: Lk 11:42.
2.to relax, loosen; pass., to be relaxed, weakened, exhausted: παρειμένας χεῖρας, He 12:12 (LXX ἀνειμ-).†

πανήγυρις.der: from G3956 (πᾶς) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά);
πανήγυρις.as:
πανήγυρις, -εως, ἡ
(< πᾶς + ἄγυρας = ἀγορά), [in LXX: Ho 2:11 (13) 9:5, Ez 46:11 (מוֹעֵד), Am 5:21 (עֲצָרָה)*;]
prop., a national festal assembly in honour of a god; hence, generally, any festal assembly: He 12:23 (for exx. in π., v. MM, xviii).†
SYN.: ἐκκλησία (q.v.), συναγωγή.

παραλλαγή.sd: transmutation (of phase or orbit), i.e. (figuratively) fickleness
παραλλαγή.der: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω);
παραλλαγή.as:
παρ-αλλαγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< παραλλάσσω), [in LXX: IV Ki 9:20 (שִׁגָּעוֹן)*;]
in various senses (LS, s.v.), change: Ja 1:17.†

πατροπαράδοτος.long: handed down by (from) one's ancestors, inherited.
πατροπαράδοτος.der: from G3962 (πατήρ) and a derivative of G3860 (παραδίδωμι) (in the sense of handing over or down);
πατροπαράδοτος.as:
*† πατρο-παρά-δοτος, -ον
(< πατήρ, παραδίδωμι),
handed down from one's fathers, inherited: I Pe 1:18 (Diod., al.).†

παρεισφέρω.long: I contribute besides, bring in besides, smuggle in.
παρεισφέρω.sd: to bear in alongside, i.e. introduce simultaneously
παρεισφέρω.as:
* παρ-εισ-φέρω,
to bring in or supply besides: σπουδὴν π. (late Gk. for cl. σ. ποιεῖσθαι; cf. Deiss., BS, 361), II Pe 1:5.†

παρεισάγω.long: I bring in secretly, am at hand.
παρεισάγω.sd: to lead in aside, i.e. introduce surreptitiously
παρεισάγω.as:
* παρ-εισ-άγω,
1.to lead in by one's side, bring forward, introduce.
2. In late writers, to introduce or bring in secretly: II Pe 2:1.†

παρανομία.as:
παρανομία, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ps 36 (37):7 (מְזִמָּה), etc.;]
law-breaking, transgression: II Pe 2:16.†

παρεισδύω.long: I enter secretly, come in by stealth.
παρεισδύω.sd: to settle in alongside, i.e. lodge stealthily
παρεισδύω.der: from G3844 (παρά) and a compound of G1519 (εἰς) and G1416 (δύνω);
παρεισδύω.as:
* παρ-εισ-δύω
(also -δύνω),
to slip in secretly, steal in: παρεισεδύησαν (vulgar aor.; pass. for act., Bl., § 19, 2), Ju 4 (cf. also MM, xix).†

Πάτμος.long: Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean sea, south-west of Ephesus.
Πάτμος.sd: Patmus, an islet in the Mediterranean
Πάτμος.as:
Πάτμος, -ου, ἡ,
Patmos, an island in the Ægean Sea: Re 1:9.†

πάρδαλις.as:
πάρδαλις, -εως, ἡ,
[in LXX for נָמֵר, Ca 4:8, Ho 13:7, Is 11:6, al.;]
a panther, leopard: Re 13:2.†
